milestone: OSHA masking v3: own-employer fragments next to [EMPLOYER] (task F, masking review)
choice: the user chose own-employer residue only (not other companies' names), about CAD 0.6-1.0

review_before.method: local scan of landing osha_sir/v2 against the raw archive (scratchpad scripts; counts and anonymized shapes only, no names printed)

other_companies_not_masked.note: left as known residue by the user's choice; most of the 155 have no company context (places, brands, ordinary names)

rule.code: sentinelops.osha.absorb_fragments / own_fragment, via mask(..., fragments=True); minimize(masking_version='v3')
rule.absorbs: a token directly before or after [EMPLOYER] that is (a) initials of consecutive words of that report's employer name (G&H, G & H, J.B., ABC) or (b) a capitalized word of that name that isn't a business word or a state; repeated until nothing changes
rule.never: lowercase words, other companies' words, business words (Inc, Company, the, a), state names

landing_v3.kind: a delta of v2: only the 17 changed reports, full records, in reports/changed.jsonl (13,498 bytes) plus manifest.json; Silver keeps each report's latest landed copy

embed.note: exactly the 17 changed documents, found by their document hash

not_changed: the deployed agent's packaged documents (osha_assistant v1 carries v2 texts until a v2 of the agent, with D's second layer)

regression.fix: osha_answer_eval takes its question sets as a job parameter (question_sets, default eval_v3_identity,eval_v2), so a run can override it; the rerun uses the identity set only, which is what a masking regression needs
regression.process_note: the rerun was started by a command chain that continued past a failing unit test (tests/test_agent.py compared the literal parameter); the test now resolves job-parameter defaults, and all 149 tests pass. The deployed configuration was correct
